claims: {{canonicalName}} is a bodyweight deep-squat-base access drill: establish an owned comfortable squat, place elbows inside the knees if available, apply gentle outward pry pressure or a small deliberate weight shift, then return or exit under control.

It excludes a squat-to-stand transition, a Cossack or lateral lunge, loaded squat, static test, unsupported forced end-range hold, and any overhead reach unless that reach is explicitly assigned as a variant.
Stance, toe angle, support, depth, duration, gentle prying/shift, and an optional reach are delivery dimensions only after the squat base and controlled exit are fixed.
A deliberate stand-up/hinge/reach sequence changes the primary ordered task and is not silently merged into this card.
The card records foot, ankle, knee, hip, pelvis, trunk, shoulder, elbow, and wrist task roles without diagnosing restriction or asserting a muscle-isolation outcome.
Squat depth and loading alter joint moments; this low-load access drill does not establish a universal stance, depth, or tissue effect.
Stance width and foot angle affect knee, hip, and trunk motion/loading in squat tasks, so the candidate uses a self-selected comfortable stance rather than a universal angle.
A valid repetition or exposure retains foot contact and trunk organisation, applies only gentle deliberate pressure or shift, and exits under control rather than collapsing or forcing range.
Difficulty fields describe the squat-access task’s coordination and physical demand only, never athlete skill, proficiency, age, or classification.
Deep flexion, foot contact, trunk control, and self-managed range make the task coordination-sensitive despite low external load; independent calibration remains required.
Acute stretching or mobility effects depend on type, dose, timing, and subsequent activity; no universal readiness, recovery, or performance outcome is claimed.
Track duration, breath, range, stance, foot contact, support, shift/pry, symptoms, and downstream squat/jump/lunge work rather than assigning a universal recovery rule.
Stable non-slip footing, clearance to enter and exit, optional stable support, and clear stop communication are practical safeguards.
Selection is determined by current workout inputs and the exact task, not an exercise-card population or skill label.
No source establishes a universal Deep Squat Pry dose, depth, stance, rest, or readiness threshold.
Use a conservative quality-limited candidate exposure and stop before pain, pinching, dizziness, breath-holding, lost foot contact, or persistent compensation.
Instructions must name self-selected foot position, comfortable squat depth, optional elbow contact, gentle pry/shift, breathing, quality boundary, and controlled exit.
Reduce depth, range, duration, or use stable support before forcing heel contact or knee position.
Appropriate instruction, supervision, environment, and progressive exposure are safeguards.
Stop for sharp or increasing pain, new neurologic/circulation/breathing/dizziness symptoms, unsafe support/surface, inability to exit, or persistent quality loss after a simpler setup.
Use {{canonicalName}} only when its exact low-load squat-access task fits a session objective and downstream demands; it does not promise flexibility, injury prevention, treatment, or transfer.
Any change to support, depth, stance, reach, shift, duration, tempo, dose, or substitution reruns selection, logistics, duration, fatigue, and validation.
Athlete support should show an owned foot-supported squat, gentle pressure or shift, breathing, controlled exit, range option, and stop prompt in plain language.
Captions, transcript, still sequence, audio description, exact variant match, and media quality remain human-review requirements.

Coach support should include floor and exit checks, the assigned squat base, foot contact, knee and trunk observation, duration/range record, compensation threshold, and escalation for unresolved symptoms.
Do not diagnose a restriction or replace a missing task with a generic deep squat.

Candidate supports include stable hand support, an elevated target or reduced range, a still sequence, captions, transcript, audio description, and a reviewed substitution when the squat base is inaccessible.
These supports do not establish individual readiness or automatically preserve identity after a task change.
A declared reach, support, range, tempo, or pause can be a variant or modifier of an exact squat-pry base.

Squat-to-Stand with Reach has a hinge/stand/reach ordered cycle; Cossack and lateral lunge change stance or foot sequence; loaded squats and tests change loading or intent and are not automatic substitutions.

Three inherited direct YouTube URLs are retained solely as unverified candidates; no playback, embedding, exact task match, captions, accessibility, quality, safety, reviewer, or approval claim is made.
Privacy-enhanced embed URLs are generated for review workflow only and remain non-embeddable until human verification.

assessmentSummary.identity: Deep Squat Pry is a bodyweight deep-squat-base access drill. Establish a self-selected comfortable squat with feet supported; elbows may contact the inner knees. Apply gentle outward pry pressure or a small deliberate side-to-side weight shift while breathing, then return or exit under control. This is not a squat-to-stand sequence, Cossack, lateral lunge, loaded squat, static test, forced hold, or unassigned reach.
currentCardFindings: Source 61 lacks an exact exposure boundary, stance/depth/support contract, fatigue and logistics tracking, variant distinctions, calibration evidence, and review gates.

Migration 390 already resolves Deep Squat Pry with Reach as the same deep-squat-pry identity with reach/thoracic-rotation delivery dimensions; this card retains that traceability without making an unassigned reach selectable.
Three legacy YouTube URLs are preserved as unverified candidate media only.

proposedTaxonomy.laterality: bilateral foot-supported base; record an intentional side shift separately
proposedTaxonomy.intent: low-load comfortable squat-position access and control without forced end range

proposedDosage.progressWhen: the assigned depth, breath, foot contact, and exit remain controlled without symptoms

coachCues: Choose a comfortable stance and depth
Use elbows only for gentle pressure
Breathe and make a small shift or pry
athleteInstructions: Set your feet and lower into a comfortable squat
Gently open or shift without forcing
Stand, reset, or stop before quality changes

calibrationEvidence.basis: squat stance/depth biomechanics, safe progressive-training guidance, acute-stretching evidence boundaries, legacy comparison, and inherited metadata-unverified media candidates
calibrationEvidence.uncertainty: No source establishes a unique Deep Squat Pry score, dose, recovery period, clinical outcome, or transfer effect.

assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Retain one candidate-only Deep Squat Pry identity. Treat declared reach, support, stance, range, tempo, and pause as explicit variants or modifiers. Keep Squat-to-Stand with Reach, Cossack, lateral lunge, loaded squats, static assessments, and forced end-range holds separate.
